fields.outcome: Authors can maintain related documentation in multiple languages and readers can move between language versions.
fields.scope: Add linked language variants to documentation specifications and generated output, stable section identifiers independent of translated headings or numbering, locale-keyed journey targets reusable across language captures, and an optional report of UI strings that do not match the capture locale. Language fallback and matching rules remain design questions.
fields.acceptance: A language variant can link to its sibling document. Equivalent sections retain the same explicit anchor across translations. One journey can resolve target labels from locale-specific resources. A capture can report candidate untranslated UI strings for review without treating heuristics as authoritative translation failures.
fields.verification: Cover schema validation and generated language links, compare anchors across translated fixtures, execute one locale-keyed journey against at least two locale fixtures, and test untranslated-string report output and limitations.
fields.risks: String mismatch heuristics can report proper names or user data as untranslated and miss translated strings. Reports must be advisory and must not expose captured secrets.
fields.source: Consumer feedback supplied by the user on 2026-11-03; scope and acceptance remain discovery-stage proposals.

criteria.expectation: A specification can declare a sibling document per language and generated documents expose usable links to available variants.
Section anchors can be explicitly shared across language variants and do not depend on translated headings or chapter numbers.
Journey targets can resolve accessible names from locale-keyed resources so the same journey definition works across configured languages.
Capture can optionally report candidate UI strings inconsistent with the selected locale, with findings clearly marked as heuristic.
